topic: Dissertation Literature Review: The Synthesis Matrix

copy.instagram:
Staring at a pile of 40 papers and feeling like your lit review is just a glorified list of summaries? We’ve all been there—the 3 AM realization that you’ve written a book report instead of a critical analysis. 

Stop summarizing and start synthesizing. Here is how to pivot:

Slide 1: The 2:2 Trap. Stop organizing by author or year. It reads like a list, not an argument.

Slide 2: The 1st Class Blueprint. Use a Synthesis Matrix. Group your research by themes, theoretical debates, and methodological limitations.

Slide 3: The Secret Sauce. Your job isn’t just to repeat what they said—it’s to point out where they disagree and where the research stops. That’s your ‘gap’.

Save this for when you’re knee-deep in reading and need a roadmap to get back on track. If the synthesis is still feeling messy, link in bio for a chat. We’ll get it sorted.

copy.facebook:
Is your dissertation literature review feeling like a never-ending cycle of 'book reports'? It’s the most common hurdle for Master’s students, but it’s entirely fixable.

If you’re organizing your chapters by author or year, you’re missing the chance to demonstrate critical analysis. To hit those 1st-class marks, you need to shift to thematic coding:

• Stop listing: Compare how different studies approach the same problem.
• Highlight the tension: Where do the methodologies clash? What are the limitations in their sampling?
• Define the gap: Your entire review should be building toward the one thing the current research hasn't answered yet.

Don’t burn yourself out trying to fix a structural issue alone. I’ve helped hundreds of students untangle their research arguments and get their flow back on track.
